title: Bessie Smith raised in her mother's house
summary: Austin says Bessie Smith grew up with her and learned to sing by imitating Ma Rainey at a carnival.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Well, I worked with either London than I did anybody else, so I guess I would probably have to say that. But Maureen was a singer that, when I was a little girl...
I like that deep quality that she had, that big, heavy voice. Maureen?
When I was a little girl, I mean a little girl... What's her name there who worked for Columbia?
Bessie Smith. Bessie Smith. Bessie Smith lived right next door to me.
She was raised in my mother's house. She was raised in my mother's house. We were raised together. Well, you know, Bessie made every record that I put out.
And way Bessie learned how to sing. Maureen and Paureen, that's her husband.

They used to come there with a carnival, and it happened in a vacant lot. And Bessie and I used to sit out in the back of the carnival because we couldn't go in. Yeah. We'd sit out there, and Maureen would sing, Oh, these dogs of mine, that's a little torture. Yeah, I remember that. And we would sit back out there, and she would imitate Maureen singing. She would learn. That's the way she learned how to sing. And she was here with me just before she went away. See, she went down to Memphis, and her brother was driving in the car and had an accident.
